A separate read-only visibility pass records one entry per exact-schema-17 report item that is unavailable or unknown, including publisher feature IDs the maintained first-party inventories cannot name. It returns null unless the project is a non-array object whose own `schemaVersion` data property is exactly 12 and the report is an incompatible soundscaper-project report retaining at least one unavailable or unknown item, so a compatible project costs one project and one report property read and a future schema returns before any traversal. The pass is strictly read-only: it never projects, bypasses, mutates, or reprojects anything, and it returns one deep-frozen index. It does read canonical state, walking the live canonical current project rather than any playback projection; only mutation is excluded. Every named property it reads on project data goes through an own-data-property descriptor check, so a project-supplied accessor in a named position is treated as absent rather than invoked or thrown on, but array membership is read by ordinary element access and forEach, so that guarantee covers named property reads only and not array traversal. Its read surface is container membership plus object identity and inertness: rack, clip, and effect IDs, effect type, track type to separate audio from label and video tracks, clip kind, and the `effectsActive`, `enabled`, and `bypassed` flags; effect params, context, state, and opaque payloads are not read. Attribution follows the declared requirement rather than an inference from an unrecognized feature ID, and never the outcome of playback qualification or integrity admission: an item carrying a fallback is attributed by its declared closed role even when that descriptor would not qualify for playback, so a `video-clip-render-v1` descriptor reported unknown is still indexed and still labelled `Replaced during editor playback` although the clip role qualifies for editor playback only when availability is unavailable. Subject to the identity skips disclosed below, project-audio-mix-v1 names the canonical objects that role's projection would replace, namely every non-label, non-video track rack, every mixer group and send bus, the master rack under its fixed `master` identity, and every non-video timeline clip; project-video-render-v1 names timeline video tracks as well as timeline video clips, because the projection collapses both and naming only the clips would leave a video-track-only project reporting nothing; video-clip-render-v1 names only its exact target clip ID. For an item that declares no fallback, the two first-party effect capability IDs collect only effect types outside the maintained registry, so `registered` is always false on those channels: a maintained type already has its own first-party placeholder section, and collecting it would spend the shared ceiling on rows the notice discards. Both effect channels honour the same inertness gates as the sibling bypass projections, the audio channel skipping a rack with `effectsActive` false and an effect with `enabled` false or `bypassed` true, the video channel skipping an effect with `enabled` false, which is its whole gate because a persisted video effect carries no bypass flag. The two channels are not equally reachable: schema-12 validation runs normalizeVideoEffects over every timeline and Project Bin video clip, so a foreign video effect type cannot exist in a project that opens and the video-effect channel is reachable in principle but not by any project that opens, while persisted audio effect validation admits any non-empty type string, making unregistered types an audio-rack phenomenon in practice. Attributable is set only once a channel actually names at least one object: a declared fallback that matches nothing, such as a `targetClipId` no timeline clip matches or a video role on a project with no video track and no video clip, is recorded unattributable with an empty object list, as is every requirement no channel can name objects for, the normal case for a publisher feature ID with no fallback, so the notice states that the affected objects cannot be identified instead of rendering nothing; an object dropped for exhausted budget still counts as named, an object whose identity could not be read does not. One shared lower-only 4,096-object ceiling with a test seam is spent across the whole index in enumeration order. It bounds the retained list rather than the traversal: enumeration continues after exhaustion, and the whole index is recomputed per document snapshot for any incompatible schema-12 document, so an oversized project pays the walk on every snapshot. Deliberately unlike the maintained bypass projections, which reject, exhaustion truncates and discloses through a per-requirement omitted count, a truncated flag on the index, and a localized omission line, because a truncated read-only advisory list cannot leave an effect audible while a truncated bypass would, so an oversized project degrades this list instead of failing. The pass is otherwise total: the only throw is a RangeError for a seam value that is not a non-negative safe integer or that would raise the production ceiling. A non-object project, a non-data descriptor, and a missing, empty, or over-long stable ID or object type no longer reject, and the 256-character stable-ID and 128-character object-type ceilings skip the object rather than truncating the value or throwing, because this pass runs on the document-snapshot path where a throw would blank the editor and schema-12 validation bounds no identifier or type length at all. Disclosure of those skips is uneven: an effect skipped for an unreadable identity is counted in the omitted count, while a track, bus, or clip skipped for an unreadable ID is dropped silently, so a fallback list can be short by an unnamed object without saying so, and a clip whose kind is absent or over-long is still listed under the generic object type `clip`. The index is derived in the document snapshot from the live current project plus the retained activation-time report, so it follows later edits; it is not persisted, is not stored in per-tab metadata, and never passes through projectForPlayback. The maintained workspace notice renders it as one additional control-free section under the matching requirement, keyed per row by channel, location, scope, owner, and object ID because a track and a clip may legitimately share an ID under V10, which enforces ID uniqueness only within a collection. That section shows only newly visible state, namely canonical objects a rendered fallback replaces and effects whose type is outside the maintained registry; maintained registered effect types remain the existing first-party audio and video inventories' subject matter, and the notice's registered-effect filter is now a redundant safeguard rather than a live deduplication because the pass no longer collects a maintained effect type at all. An attributable requirement with no newly visible and no omitted object renders no section. This control grants no new capability. It adds no generic unavailable-feature placeholder, engine projection, or bypass, so bypass remains exactly the two maintained first-party slices and nothing is substituted into the engine project, and it changes no activation, read-only enforcement, persistence, offline render, export, or delivery behavior. No listed object becomes controllable, selectable, or actionable; the post-open notice remains informational and control-free; and naming an object authorizes nothing for third-party or unknown features. Structural naming does not establish publisher authenticity, does not discover, load, or execute feature code, does not evaluate what an unavailable feature would actually do to a named object, and does not extend attribution to any capability ID beyond the first-party audio and video effect slices.

Poster and thumbnail cache publication resolves the retained original by storage key and derives its repository-trusted current SHA-256 plus media-content token. A content-addressed key binds the original storage key and digest, the closed poster/thumbnail type and normalized non-negative source time, and a versioned recipe. Save computes the output digest and revalidates the original digest/token immediately before publication; IndexedDB atomically publishes the payload and scalar companion, and failed publication removes staged OPFS output. Load derives identity from the current original, requires the payload/companion binding scalars to match on IndexedDB, and verifies stored output size and SHA-256. A well-formed row from a different original generation is a cache miss even when its digest is unchanged; legacy or unbound rows also miss, while malformed pairs, bindings, and body integrity reject. IndexedDB exact deletion and media-asset cascade require each selected payload to match its scalar companion before any row is deleted, then dispose only paths re-projected from validated payloads after commit; mismatch aborts without OPFS disposal, so a corrupt companion path cannot delete an unrelated original. An explicit recipe deletion selector matches only its normalized recipe ID/version, while an omitted recipe selects all revisions. New video-source imports and maintained read-write .scape imports persist null posterStorageKey and thumbnailStorageKey values, maintained source-update commands cannot author them, future read-only imports remain opaque, desktop recipient binding excludes legacy locator values, and managed source declarations omit them. currentControls.summary: The renderer has context isolation, no Node integration, a sandbox, and a frozen input-validating v1 bridge. Its shared-project methods are bounded, pathless list, read, bundle, commit, delete, and managed-media transfer operations for the closed canonical-PCM and retained-original-video encodings whose arguments and return values are independently sanitized in main. Its linked-original lifecycle methods use closed kind-specific pathless DTOs. A release request is a closed exact kind, locator ID, and revision expressed as own enumerable data fields; missing, scalar, accessor-backed, or open requests fail before IPC. Audio and video load requests carry mandatory Boolean range and playback modes respectively: whole-Blob materialization requires false, while ranged access requires true and a non-null exact locator revision. Main and preload independently validate the mode, returned revision, profile-bound descriptor, safe size, canonical pathless URL, and kind-specific MIME/name contract and retire a descriptor that cannot cross the boundary. Cooperative startup reconciliation accepts at most 128 unique exact locator/revision pairs; main independently validates shape and known exact revisions but does not authenticate inventory completeness. Reconciliation can mutate only startup-loaded private locator metadata and never receives paths or deletes external files. Main admits at most four active managed-source uploads and four active reads across the shared-project bridge service, enforces 64 GiB source-body and 4 MiB chunk or read ceilings, and exposes descriptors rather than filesystem paths; upload sessions and linked-original reads remain owner-bound for authorization and revocation. The same bridge exposes nine independently validated, owner-scoped external-video methods for capabilities, begin, input write, input close, execute, stat, bounded range read, delete, and cancel. Those calls carry opaque operation ids, exact closed plans, and at-most-1-MiB chunks; executable paths, filesystem paths, and argv never cross into renderer authority.

The active desktop localAssistance v1 bridge is frozen and pathless. Preload and main independently admit only opaque 40-hex job, claim and stream identities; the closed fifteen-operation vocabulary; exact model versions and artifact digests; S30/F31 selection fences; bounded media-type-specific input claims and output reservations; correlated results, typed unavailable outcomes and monotonic progress. Input bytes cross through one exact MessagePort reservation bound to role, media type, byte length and SHA-256 and land in main-private per-job staging; output bytes return through a separately negotiated authenticated MessagePort without exposing a path. Main redacts filesystem and native error detail before rejection. Cancellation and release stop negotiated transfers, await active helper quiescence and only then remove private staging. Only an installed authenticated Parakeet transducer executes speech-recognition through the verified Sherpa runtime. Every other closed operation returns adapter-unavailable, and absent compatible model/runtime state returns its typed unavailable result without an implicit install, upstream fetch, alternate model or fabricated output. Model installation and operation launch remain explicit menu actions. Explicit reviewed acceptance revalidates the complete current S30/F31 selection fence through an AssistanceProposalSession, stages one canonical content-addressed transcript body, and commits its strict assistance-asset reference with a deterministic ordinary label track as one undoable project command. Stale selection or reference authority refuses; body or command failure rolls back newly owned body publication; a whole rerun replaces the owned transcript instead of merging inferred text. Current-format .scape custody authenticates and transfers the external body with its source binding, while AUP4 explicitly reports omission. Manual and owner-lab qualification is documentary and nonblocking; it remains pending and unprovisioned, with no accepted owner result. Licensing permission, catalog signature, artifact digest, runtime and platform compatibility, selected-media authority, storage integrity, and explicit consent all remain hard fail-closed gates.

Selected Framescaper F31 alone mounts the main-owned persistent-services V3 runtime after settings load, delegates native project behavior through its immutable exact V28/V14 foundation, and exposes the frozen framescaperDesktop.v1.nativeServices capability/snapshot, queue lifecycle, durable-root selection and revalidation, watch CRUD/reconciliation, scratch settlement, verified publication/checkpoint, external-display and preference methods plus authenticated frame and live-render MessagePorts. Preload and main independently validate closed pathless queue/root/watch projections and exact requests, reject destination traversal, authenticate the current renderer owner, and never return filesystem paths, SQLite handles, Electron objects, executable identities or raw media. Main owns the V3 database, lease-fenced queue/root/watch/scratch repositories, checkpoint recovery, publication fences, proxy-output broker, display session and exact F31/V14/V20 project authority and disposes them on shutdown. The renderer closes, canonicalizes and fingerprints the exact V14 plan before request construction; preload preserves the bounded closed declaration, and main reauthenticates the plan, current project, source bodies, timing and carrier before queue admission. The maintained native render route carries one evaluated-RGBA stream plus optional float32 audio, while helper-owned image-sequence work seals an exact regular-file output tree under scratch and main revalidates it immediately before broker-relative no-clobber destination publication. Authenticated broker trees are non-empty, so a concurrent completed broker winner cannot be replaced; however Node 26 exposes no portable directory RENAME_NOREPLACE primitive, and an external same-user process can race an empty destination into the absence-check/rename window. Cross-process atomic no-clobber is therefore not qualified. The watch flow settles a stable pathless landing, commits the exact Project Bin mutation before acknowledgement, then schedules optional proxy work; restart recovery resumes proxy-only work without replaying the project mutation. Queue execution is constructed only when exact project/source authority, a main-owned physical-capacity authority, an authenticated payload and accepted readiness all admit it. Before each dispatch pass capacity samples host parallelism, free memory and scratch, deducts running and durable reservations, and closes CPU, process-tree RSS, scratch, minimum-free-space and hardware-backend budgets. The repository alone claims admitted rows as running inside one immediate writer transaction; the dispatcher executes only those claims, defaults to two concurrent jobs within the closed one-through-four bound, and wakes deferred rows only after active completion or an explicit queue/preference event. Activation is not qualification, and that smoke is not manual qualification: actual packaged cameras, microphones, operating-system picker and loopback behavior, encoder and timing behavior, teardown performance, signing, and long-session performance remain unqualified while the real-device and owner-lab evidence stays provisional and unprovisioned.

With that gate false, the controller returns `unavailable` with reason `roadmap-gate` without performing a desktop handshake or guest open. Main selects one immutable profile and all four profiles share at most 128 pending or live capability slots per owner, reserved before the first file-open await. `materialized-v1` retains a non-raiseable 512 MiB aggregate declared-byte ceiling per owner. Canonical terminal Scape projects use the independent `scape-range-v1` admission of at most four capabilities and 65 GiB aggregate declared bytes both globally and per owner. Count reserves before open and bytes charge after stat but before publication. A failed candidate or retirement cleanup retains its range charge and fences new range admission. Wrong-owner release refuses without revealing, removing, or closing the capability. Correct release and expiry for the expiring profiles synchronously remove it from lookup before draining its handle; linked-original ranges deliberately remain owner-pinned without wall-clock expiry. Navigation, renderer loss, window close, and shutdown fence the affected owner or store before draining every admitted open and handle close; delayed dialog, open, or stat completion closes without publication. Partial multi-file registration drains every rollback release and reports primary plus cleanup failures. OS-open paths remain serially deduplicated at one visible queue head. With four real Scape descriptors admitted globally, the fifth refuses before open and remains queued; one acknowledged release redispatches it. A renderer-send failure releases its descriptor before reporting and removing that head. Transient count or aggregate-byte pressure is retryable without eviction, but an individually oversized file is not. Revocation and shutdown attempt every close before rejecting on cleanup failure, and shutdown permanently refuses new admission.

A linked-video playback request is a closed pathless DTO with mandatory playback mode and non-null exact locator revision. Main first requires the current pathname stat to match the persisted device, inode, size, modification-time, and change-time identity, then opens an owner-scoped handle and independently requires that handle to match the same identity before publishing a `linked-video-range-v1` descriptor. Pathname replacement during admission fails closed, and replacement after admission cannot retarget the opened handle. One capability is limited to 512 MiB; the linked-original admission gate shared with audio permits at most 128 capabilities and 64 GiB of declared bytes globally and per owner plus 16 active requests globally. Playback capabilities have no wall-clock expiry while their renderer-document owner is live. The protocol permits `HEAD` and one start-based closed or open-ended `GET` range, caps every response at 4 MiB, and rejects full-body GET, suffix, multiple, oversized, and EOF-overrun requests. Success and ordinary seek cancellation drain only the request slot and preserve the capability; inner stream failure retires it. Explicit release, owner revocation, navigation, renderer loss, window close, and shutdown remove it from lookup and drain its request and handle. Main and preload validate the closed mode, exact revision, profile, video MIME, name, safe size, and canonical pathless URL and roll back malformed responses. The renderer port repeats those descriptor checks and uses exact closed GET ranges. The resolver checks exact project/source binding metadata before privileged I/O, verifies length and MIME, hashes the full handle sequentially through at-most-4-MiB ranges with exact `206`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Content-Range`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, and body-byte agreement, and rereads the exact binding and CAS fence before returning only a media URL and one-shot release. Cancellation, metadata or binding drift, malformed responses, and digest mismatch release the capability; simultaneous verification and cleanup failures remain aggregated.

A linked-audio range request is a closed pathless DTO with mandatory range mode and a non-null exact locator revision. Main requires the current pathname stat and the newly opened owner-scoped handle to match the persisted device, inode, size, modification-time, and change-time identity before publishing a `linked-audio-range-v1` descriptor. Pathname replacement during admission fails closed, and later movement, deletion, or replacement cannot retarget the opened handle. Audio shares the linked-original gate with video: at most 128 capabilities and 64 GiB of declared bytes globally and per owner, 512 MiB per file, 16 active requests globally, and 4 MiB per response. The owner-pinned capability has no wall-clock expiry. Main, preload, and renderer validate the exact revision, range mode, profile, safe size, canonical URL, and either the maintained WAV/RF64 MIME/name contract or an exact `.aif` or `.aiff` name with `audio/aiff`; `.aifc` is not admitted. The renderer issues only exact closed ranges and validates `206`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Content-Range`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, and body-byte agreement. The resolver checks exact binding metadata before privileged I/O, hashes the stable opened handle sequentially, and rereads the binding and CAS fence before maintained-container inspection and canonical PCM chunk reads proceed without another whole-original Blob. Classic AIFF requires FORM/AIFF with structurally consistent COMM and SSND chunks and accepts signed big-endian integer PCM at 8, 16, 24, or 32 bits. The canonical first-party AIFF-C profile requires FORM/AIFC, one four-byte FVER v1 (`0xA2805140`) before an exact 44-byte COMM, 32-bit `fl32`, the exact Pascal compression name `32-bit floating point`, and structurally consistent SSND geometry; the first-party label describes the maintained fixture, not authenticated provenance: admission is producer-neutral and accepts any producer emitting that exact tuple. Broader, compressed, and other AIFC profiles reject; broader third-party interoperability and producer provenance are unqualified. Acquisition cancellation, drift before publication, malformed responses, digest mismatch, and session completion release once, with cleanup failures aggregated. For maintained playback, one demand-loaded provider lazily owns one provider-owned stable PCM read session, retaining the same exact-revision opened handle, one full-container digest, and one parsed descriptor across serialized random or sequential chunk reads. Every chunk rechecks the complete alias group and exact binding before and after decoding. Per-read engine or stream cancellation is local; binding or alias drift, malformed or corrupt range data, and provider retirement are terminal. Maintained provider replacement, failed activation, project switch, project or source deletion and clear, rollback, and controller or store disposal await exact-once release before backing cleanup and aggregate cleanup failures with the primary failure. Initial selection and binding still materialize the whole external container under the 512 MiB tier. This does not establish packaged-executable or operating-system behavior, source-container metadata preservation, a content-frozen, restart-stable, or cross-process lease, audible/device playback, broader or compressed AIFC, third-party AIFC interoperability and provenance, the `.aifc` extension, or reference-scale qualification. Same-inode mutation during or after verification remains unfenced. Four-MiB transport bounds do not bound retained Float32 arrays, parsed metadata, decoder allocation, or process RSS.

This control applies only to main-assigned `materialized-v1` descriptors. Authoritative main-process admission limits their aggregate active declared selected-file bytes to a non-raiseable 512 MiB per committed-document owner before publication. The preload validates the exact materialized profile, name, MIME, safe size, and canonical profile-bearing URL. The renderer repeats profile admission before fetch and rejects any Scape name, canonical Scape MIME, `scape-range-v1`, `linked-audio-range-v1`, or `linked-video-range-v1` descriptor instead of materializing it. For admitted materialized reads it requires exact declared Content-Length, emitted-byte, and final Blob-size agreement and reads only the response body stream. Retained parts are copied and split at the non-raiseable 16 MiB platform media-chunk limit. The materializer forwards the caller's AbortSignal, promptly races and cancels a stalled body read with its exact reason, and never calls response.blob(). A scoped descriptor batch releases every capability after its callback on success, failure, or cancellation, while request abort destroys the protocol file stream. This is a bounded whole-Blob tier, not a bound on decoder amplification or whole-process RSS; Scape and linked-original audio/video ranges are excluded and handled by their separately admitted range profiles.

currentControls.summary: A user-selected target becomes a short-lived single-use token; sequential one-MiB chunks are checked against an exact length and committed by synced same-directory rename with abort cleanup. An exact session may declare only one fixed 32-byte final-prefix patch: the owner-bound operation exposes no caller-selected offset, requires every declared byte first, replaces only position zero exactly once without changing the session byte count, and blocks finish after a missing or failed patch.

Only project save capabilities may select bounded streaming mode. Main rejects writes above the archive-admitted maximum, waits for an active chunk acknowledgement before abort cleanup, and removes sessions on navigation, renderer loss, window close, or shutdown; explicit finish remains the sync-and-rename commit boundary.

A dedicated `audio-pcm-mix` purpose permits only WAV, AIFF, BWF, and BW64 target names without granting generic audio targets maximum-bounded streaming authority. The maintained direct PCM route admits one mix only when its plan has one output and `realtime-stream`. The largest constructible RIFF layout under the 32-bit RIFF-size field is 4,294,967,302 bytes; its next mono int16 frame selects RF64 at 4,294,967,340 bytes. Exact integer AIFF, AIFF-C float, odd PCM padding, and trailing ID3 metadata use that same encoder geometry. BWF requires `audio/wav`, `.wav`, and one positive safe-integer planned file byte count at or below 65 GiB. Admission requires an explicit valid sample rate, 1–32 channels, a nonnegative safe-integer frame count, object metadata, a marker array, and null-or-object iXML and CART. It recomputes the automatic RIFF/RF64 layout with `inspectWavLayout` from the same encoder options used by streaming: sample rate, channel count, frame count, integer precision, BEXT, metadata, markers, iXML, and CART. The maintained exact direct compressed whole-mix route is closed to one mix and the seven canonical built-in FFmpeg formats: `mp3` with `audio/mpeg` and `.mp3`; `flac` with `audio/flac` and `.flac`; `ogg-vorbis` with `audio/ogg; codecs=vorbis` and `.ogg`; `opus` with `audio/ogg; codecs=opus` and `.opus`; `wavpack` with `audio/x-wavpack` and `.wv`; `mp2` with `audio/mpeg` and `.mp2`; and `aac-m4a` with `audio/mp4` and `.m4a`. Every admitted plan has an 8–384 kHz sample rate, positive output frames, a canonical nonempty range, exact normalized settings, no compressed file-size claim, and no archive. A `realtime-stream` plan must retain its maintained memory reason and exact four-byte-per-output-sample plan. Realtime-stream rendering maps and resamples before staging and gives FFmpeg preserve geometry. A centrally admitted offline plan must pass exact revalidation of its single-mix range, tail, input and output geometry, mapping, planner thresholds, pre-roll, and reported graph latency, and its complete central offline-output admission must recompute exactly. Its non-raiseable 256 MiB ceiling covers exact useful-binary context and crop output, not end-to-end memory. Offline rendering resamples first, validates exact `Float32Array` source geometry, stages unmapped input-width PCM, and gives FFmpeg the canonical mapping, so either strategy applies mapping exactly once. FLAC alone stages an integer WAV at the requested 16- or 24-bit depth; the staging encoder owns requested dither and FFmpeg dither is disabled. Every non-FLAC format stages Float32 WAV. FFmpeg dither is enabled exactly when the normalized sample format is not `float32`, dither is not `none`, and the format is not FLAC; this includes integer WavPack and explicitly dither-enabled lossy settings, while float WavPack disables it. Realtime temporary preflight retains its output-width Float32 payload claim and its nonpersistent 96 MiB refusal. Offline preflight takes the maximum of the required temporary bytes and a raw staging PCM payload based on input channel count and frame count, using requested FLAC integer bytes or four bytes for every other format; it excludes WAV framing and padding and is not an exact staged-file size or storage reservation. The route selects a generic audio target before render but leaves it unopened; only after FFmpeg execution and a safe nonnegative stat does it open the exact-size writer. Only an ordinary offline renderer failure may reuse the same unopened target in realtime; cancellation, fallback-integrity or currentness loss, and every post-render failure do not retry. First-party rendered-fallback projection and private-provider verification finish before planning, selection, rendering, and publication without mutating canonical or global source state. Prepared Blob mode declines the direct route and preserves the legacy whole-read, final-Blob, and download path. The complete staged WAV is a `Blob` mounted through WORKERFS while the complete encoded output remains in worker MEMFS. The patched runtime reads monotonically increasing exact ranges of at most one MiB, keeps at most one read and one awaited destination write active under backpressure, and never invokes whole-file `readFile` for this output. FFmpeg stat, emitted, destination-written, and committed-result byte counts must agree; destination close precedes explicit commit, with no final renderer compressed-audio `Blob` or download publication on the direct path. Focused Node service evidence covers all seven formats in both strategies with a five-byte output, two realtime chunks or one offline chunk, exact picker contracts and staging/dither ownership, prepared-Blob fallback, and a virtual 269,484,049-byte output in 258 exact ranges. The virtual case proves transport arithmetic and backpressure only; it is not actual codec execution, codec conformance, mapping conformance, or reference-scale evidence. Custom FFmpeg, compressed stems, video, actual browser or operating-system behavior, native picker and packaged application behavior, quota, durability, crash, and power loss remain unqualified. Worker MEMFS, native or WASM codec memory, staged-input residency, renderer or browser heap, GC, process RSS, CPU, and elapsed time also remain unqualified. The 900,000-millisecond desktop prepared-target TTL leaves long offline packaged elapsed-time behavior unqualified.

The maintained exact direct MP4 route binds canonical `mp4`, `.mp4`, and `video/mp4`, and the exact direct WebM route binds canonical `webm`, `.webm`, and `video/webm`. Both use target purpose `video`, require a safe matching output name, and retain their canonical version-6 descriptor-bound and exact detached version-7 keyed plans, complete fingerprints, structural validation, SHA-256 evidence, exact stat/emitted/written/committed byte agreement, at-most-1-MiB monotonic range reads, backpressure, currentness checks, one explicit commit, and Blob-versus-direct publication boundaries. Browser V6 keeps WORKERFS/MEMFS source, staged-audio, and output ownership; browser V7 keeps its bounded SharedArrayBuffer RGBA and optional WAV rings. Desktop Soundscaper S30 inherits the exact S29 implementation, admits only the exact V7 keyed-RGBA subset, and deliberately forces the desktop provider even when WebCodecs exists. Desktop availability requires exact capability tokens plus a successful live canary for the current external ffmpeg/ffprobe pair: H.264/AAC MP4 uses `libx264` and `aac`, while WebM uses VP9/Opus through `libvpx-vp9` and `libopus`. An exact ffprobe then attests exactly two streams at indices 0 and 1, 16x16 `yuv420p` video, and 48 kHz stereo audio before availability. Renderer writes are pathless at-most-1-MiB chunks into main-private pipes; finalized output stays in main-private scratch for bounded reads and the same container, digest, byte-count, and publication checks. Bundled video, operating-system video, and AV1 remain disabled; external WebM is VP9, not AV1. Codec conformance, broad FFmpeg-version/platform behavior, packaged UI, reference-scale performance, aggregate memory, RSS, CPU, filesystem durability, crash, and power loss remain unqualified.

The maintained direct stem-archive slice owns ZIP32 and 7z Copy publication while existing format-specific controls continue to own native-container and codec conformance. Its native-PCM branch admits only an exact ZIP32 or 7z Copy archive of WAV, AIFF, or BWF stems. Before target selection both variants require `stems` mode, a nonempty output list, one positive safe-integer native output size, canonical archive MIME and extension, and matching archive entries in the same order with exact flat names and sizes. ZIP32 requires a recomputed eligible layout whose entry count, local bytes, central-directory bytes, and total archive byte length exactly match the plan. The 7z branch requires the same recomputed ZIP32 planning geometry, which may be ineligible, and an exact independently recomputed Copy archive byte length. Closed native positive admission covers WAV and BWF with `audio/wav` and `.wav`, and AIFF with `audio/aiff` and `.aiff`, in both archive formats. Compressed stems remain ZIP32-only. Its compressed branch admits the seven canonical built-ins—MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus, WavPack, MP2, and AAC/M4A—for either a canonical `realtime-stream` stem plan or a centrally admitted `offline` stem plan, captured as one owned snapshot whose fingerprint is rechecked through publication. Centrally admitted offline plans carry exact route-neutral central offline-render evidence, and the selected render strategy and strategy-aware staging bound enter that fingerprint. The realtime strategy-aware staging bound is the raw output-width `outputBytesPerRender`. The offline staging bound is `max(outputFrames × inputChannels × offlineBytesPerSample, outputBytesPerRender)`. The first term is the offline input-width staging payload; `offlineBytesPerSample` is requested FLAC integer bytes per sample or four bytes for the other six formats. The second term is the possible realtime-retry output-width staging payload: `outputFrames × outputChannels × Float32(4)`, including for FLAC. Each compressed entry receives a per-entry maximum of `max(strategy-aware staging bound, 1 MiB)`; admission computes a synthetic maximum ZIP32 layout from those maxima before target selection. That maximum is an enforced refusal boundary only, not a qualified codec expansion, conformance, or scale bound. The shared Web/Electron file-service abstraction accepts a native prepared exact-size streaming destination or compressed prepared maximum-size streaming destination and selects and opens it before any render. Native per-stem staging remains sequential, retains at most one complete stem, and its temporary-storage preflight charges the largest sequential intermediate rather than the aggregate. A direct 7z destination declares one fixed 32-byte final prefix. The Copy writer appends a zero-filled 32-byte placeholder, ordered stem bodies, and its complete next header; only after the exact stream is complete and sealed may the destination patch that fixed position-zero prefix once without changing its byte count, and commit requires the patch. Compressed temporary-storage preflight charges the same strategy-aware staging bound: realtime uses `outputBytesPerRender`, while offline uses that exact two-term maximum. It excludes WAV framing, codec output, and the aggregate legacy staging claim. Offline encoding stages the unmapped input width and leaves canonical channel mapping to FFmpeg, so mapping has one owner. The shared pass-through ZIP32 encoder bounds non-Blob input source slices to 64 KiB and awaits serial sink backpressure before accepting the next slice; the exact 7z Copy writer shares serial backpressure and one-entry-at-a-time admission. Finalization requires emitted bytes to equal the recomputed actual ZIP32 layout before it closes the destination; only after close may explicit commit require planned or actual, emitted, destination-written, and committed-result byte counts to agree. The compressed branch retains a complete staged WAV `Blob`, a complete worker MEMFS output, and one complete encoded result at a time; it recomputes actual entry sizes, preserves order, and checks all byte counts while constructing no final ZIP `Blob` and invoking no download publisher. Prepared Blob mode declines the direct route, so the existing browser Blob/download path proceeds unchanged. The focused native provider-injected Node service fixtures preflight exactly four bytes and open their exact target before rendering two ordered four-byte WAV-plan marker outputs. ZIP32 reconstructs an exact 268-byte archive. A deliberately small injected 7z route appends its zero prefix before render, retains at most one complete stem, seals and patches before commit, and matches an exact 151-byte golden archive. Both construct no final archive `Blob` and call neither the legacy archive nor download publisher. The production planner selects 7z only for ZIP32 overflow, so the small golden route is correctness rather than scale evidence. Those marker outputs isolate archive publication and are not native WAV conformance evidence. Prepared Blob mode instead proves the unchanged 272-byte legacy temporary-storage preflight, ordered archive additions, and download publication. The compressed service witness names `01-Voice.mp3` and `02-Music.mp3`, makes an eight-byte raw preflight instead of its 16-byte aggregate legacy staging claim, applies a 1,048,576-byte per-entry maximum and 2,097,406-byte maximum ZIP32 layout, then streams three- and five-byte encoded bodies into a recomputed 262-byte actual ZIP32 archive. All-seven service cases exercise both render strategies with injected encoded bytes, strategy-bound preflight, target opening before render, one encoded stem retained at a time, and no legacy archive or download publication. The shared engine fixture reconstructs an exact 468-byte four-entry archive and feeds 256 KiB through 64 KiB source slices while a blocked sink admits only one slice and one active write. Custom FFmpeg and compressed 7z stems, BW64 stems, video, inexact or reordered archives, and final-Blob direct publication remain excluded. The provider-injected evidence exercises the shared Web/Electron protocol but does not qualify File System Access, an Electron filesystem, a native picker, actual FFmpeg codec execution, codec conformance, codec expansion, renderer heap, process RSS, worker MEMFS allocation, garbage collection, CPU, elapsed time, browser or operating-system behavior, packaged UI, reference scale, quota, crash, power loss, or durability.

Shutdown synchronously rejects new target and save-session admission, drains operations admitted before the fence through any sync-and-rename commit, aborts remaining or late-opened staging, and exposes one idempotent disposal barrier that rejects on unacknowledged handle close or staging removal.

Every target and derived session is bound to one committed main-document owner. Owner revocation on main-document navigation, renderer loss, or actual window close synchronously fences admission, invalidates unconsumed targets including delayed dialog results, drains admitted begin, chunk, final-prefix-patch, finish, and abort operations through any admitted sync-and-rename commit, then aborts remaining staging. Fresh-owner session admission waits for that drain so a stale commit cannot overtake a replacement save.

Main enforces 16 outstanding product-wide targets, 4 pending or live sessions, and 65 GiB per-save and aggregate admitted bytes, covering the canonical 64 GiB expanded `.scape` envelope plus its bounded STORE/ZIP overhead. Global count and byte reservations are taken synchronously before the first await, and production ceilings expose lower-only test seams. A fail-closed bigint `statfs` available-space check completes before staging open. The check is point-in-time admission, not an operating-system reservation; charges release only after no staging was acquired, an acknowledged cleanup, or a completed commit, and a staging cleanup failure leaves them charged. A chunk or final-prefix write that fails with ENOSPC or EDQUOT is a qualified typed refusal: the staged temporary file is discarded, the session's admitted count and bytes release, and the committed target file survives, while a commit-time space failure cleans staging and names the exhausted destination. Other write failures keep the session open for retry or abort.

currentControls.summary: The separately named desktop V10 host, preload, renderer bridge, database, metadata, and lifecycle contracts require schema 18 and Framescaper ownership before operational publication. Framescaper V10 holds one renewable process-lifetime main-owned writer lease in its separate V10 storage scope and database. Startup recovers any pending metadata or body journal before authenticated renderer sessions open. Lease renewal loss fences the main, rejects new session work, aborts pre-prepare work, and drains any recovery-owned prepared publication to settlement; exact shutdown drains sessions, settles any recovery-owned prepared publication, and performs final recovery, releases only the exact lease, and then closes the database. The renderer validates one closed handshake, bounds project and sequential body geometry, transfers each proxy and timing body in at-most-4-MiB chunks, and publishes main-first before reconciling the exact claim-bound local V18 shadow. The store adapter uses main as authoritative for create, latest load, save, delete, and duplicate, keeps revision loads local, and refuses stale or mismatched witnesses. Delete and duplicate use main-first exact catalog compare-and-swap plus alias-aware shadow reconciliation. A durable delete-intent journal resumes exact local shadow and binding-row reconciliation after authoritative deletion; immutable project revisions and bodies are retained, so this slice performs no physical reclamation and never reuses a deleted project ID. The delete intent does not durably capture pre-delete locator references: abrupt process death before outer linked-original cleanup can retain main-private locator metadata for later cleanup, external files are never deleted, and crash- or power-loss locator release remains unqualified. The renderer admits one rejection-based mutation slot for publication, delete, and duplicate, and ambiguous IPC acknowledgement failures recover against authoritative main state before reporting committed, absent, or indeterminate outcomes. The historical V18/V10 artifact source and focused tests remain as an unselected compatibility-boundary fixture, but the selected package smoke no longer invokes them. No current packaged route activates, creates, migrates, or rewrites this library. Restart or reopen, revision-advance saves, proxy or timing body transfer or use, delete or duplicate, concurrent opens, lease-loss recovery, crash or power-loss recovery, interruption durability, installers, and file associations remain unqualified for the historical boundary. Framescaper V10 Windows x64 and Linux x64 remain pending-external, and no accepted packaged V10 result is retained. This separate V10 storage proves cross-product isolation from Soundscaper V10 rather than a shared mutable catalog.

The selected packaged Framescaper route authenticates exact desktop-library V20 for project schema 31, SQLite user_version 22 and scope v20 while retaining the public framescaperDesktop.v1 bridge. Generation identity remains inside the closed handshake; the parameterized exact-generation core does not merge database identities, scopes, validators or handshakes. V20 admits exact F31 and refuses earlier or unknown project and library generations. When no V20 store exists, first open opens only a settled exact V19 source read-only, authenticates each V28 document, explicitly reimports it into F31, copy-forwards managed bodies byte-for-byte through durable cursor checkpoints, and resumes idempotently after interruption without rewriting or deleting V19 or its inherited V18, V17 and V12 lineages. Renderer and main independently validate the bounded V20 handshake, F31 document digest, descriptor, and project-bound body inventory before transport. The current source-free packaged-composition test reads selected F31 through the pathless preload and an independent main session and binds canonical document bytes, digest, and the closed V20 handshake; V19/V28 remains direct immutable import evidence, and older V18/V27, V17/V20, V12/V20, and V10/V18 fixtures remain separate compatibility evidence. The configured cross-platform lease runner and workflow now target V20, but configuration and source-free package evidence do not qualify source-bearing handoff, platform durability, signing, notarization, hardware, codec or external operating-system execution; no accepted V20 packaged result is checked in.

A fresh filesystem library scope v9 uses SQLite user_version 11 and ignores rather than migrates the prior shared v8 scope, preserving its metadata schema 8, exact schema 16 catalog, and SQLite user_version 10 in place. The older v7/schema-15/user-version-9 and earlier scopes remain historical and untouched. A copied v8 database with user_version 10 placed at the v9 path is rejected without mutation instead of being migrated, adopted, or backfilled. Metadata schema 9 binds a separate opaque library entry ID to the project identity, exact schema 17, project revision, bounded byte length, SHA-256, and derived immutable revision-and-digest path. The main project store uses the canonical tagged-binary codec, enforces the non-raiseable 256 MiB document ceiling through a lower-only test seam, validates the persistence root identity, and reserves each canonical immutable path in a lease- and fencing-token-bound authoritative project-file inventory before stage creation. Before `JSON.parse` constructs an object graph, every schema receives a structural scan under raw ceilings of 101,536 JSON values and depth 130, including the worst-case tagged-binary descriptor expansion. Exact schema 17 then receives independent decoded-codec and semantic-validator ceilings of 100,000 logical nodes and depth 128 per phase. The main-owned editor service exposes lower-only seams for these limits across renderer input, loaded commit results, stored reads, and response serialization. An over-budget renderer input rejects before host commit or project staging. A loaded commit result may be rejected after the host has already published it, but neither that result nor an over-budget stored read reaches the renderer response. The lexical preflight, decoded-codec traversal, validator admission, and response serialization reset their counters and do not constitute one aggregate CPU, elapsed-time, cancellation, allocation, or RSS budget. Structural admission is qualified for canonical JSON-derived production graphs and ordinary direct objects, not arbitrary in-realm proxies or malicious injected hosts or providers. Within that scope, accessors, callable toJSON hooks, method-shadowed arrays, hidden or symbol data, cycles, exotic containers, and non-JSON scalars reject without invoking application accessors. The store writes a private file, syncs it, atomically renames it, syncs the containing directory where supported, marks the inventory row materialized, reverifies length, digest, schema, ID, and revision, and requires every catalog reference to have a materialized row before an exact plus-one catalog journal publication. The main-owned editor service runs the strict exact-schema-17 maintained-persistence-domain validator before calling host commit and therefore before project staging; it repeats validation on loaded commit results and stored reads before returning a renderer response. Core project, document, media, and graph structures are strictly checked. All audio effects must be cloneable and carry their generic identity, enabled, and parameter structure; type-specific semantic checks cover missing-effect compatibility metadata and parametric EQ, while other first- and third-party effect payload semantics are intentionally not gated. Adversarial fixtures reject invalid collection shapes, duplicate identities, dangling source or clip references, over-node and deeply nested shapes, non-enumerable or accessor-backed ordinary properties, array method shadows, non-JSON scalar values, and invalid loaded commit results. Input-side failures do not reach a host commit or project file, and the packaged runtime fixture proves both validation and structural admission are emitted and active. Lease ownership is checked before staging, before publication, and transactionally at catalog commit. The host serializes commits and renews its lease while close drains admitted work. The shared-project surface of the identity service, frozen preload, and owner-scoped IPC exposes only bounded pathless list, read, bundle, commit, delete, and managed-media transfer operations for the closed canonical-PCM and retained-original-video encodings. Main and preload independently enforce the 256 MiB document, 4 KiB identity, 10,000-summary, 64 GiB managed-source body, and 4 MiB chunk ceilings; main admits at most four active uploads and four active reads across the bridge service. Catalog summaries omit entry IDs, main-owned catalog/filesystem paths, digests, product preferences, raw `updatedAtMs` fields, leases, and fencing tokens. Renderer-owner revocation fences new work, aborts owned upload sessions, and drains admitted operations. The renderer repository repeats maintained-persistence-domain exact-schema-17 validation and canonical reserialization before local mutation, treats the shared latest document and summary list as authoritative, retains a product-local revision, source, and media shadow, and fails closed on an incomplete desktop bridge. A composed source-free editor fixture creates and autosaves in Soundscaper, discovers and bootstrap-reopens the same identity and revision from a fresh Framescaper-local store, publishes the next revision under a higher fencing token, and leaves the shared media catalog empty.

Historical pre-V18 desktop-library V9 and shared schema 17 evidence used a dedicated Linux x64 CI job to build two separate unpacked Soundscaper and Framescaper packages, then run sequential Soundscaper to Framescaper to Soundscaper processes. The current CI job is retired and no longer runs this incompatible V9/V17 source-free handoff against Framescaper V18/V10. The processes share only one isolated appData root, use separate product profiles, and the return stage reuses the Soundscaper profile. Each process waits for renderer ready, drives bounded pathless preload IPC, exact-SHA-256 verifies the expected canonical source-free schema 17 document, commits revisions 1, 2, and 3, checks the renderer summary and main-only catalog row, requires clean recovery, no stale takeover, higher fencing tokens, increasing catalog revisions, and the expected preferred product, and awaits process exit and lease release before the next stage. Combined with the composed editor fixture, this closes only the generic packaged source-free preload/IPC/multi-process/executable lifecycle gap. It does not qualify packaged controller autosave or tab activation; source-bearing bytes, playback, or managed media; concurrent opens; crash or stale takeover; interruption or power loss; parent-, database-, or project-root path identity; installers or file associations; or Windows, macOS, or ARM64. Third-party activation gating and legacy Soundscaper library migration remain deliberately outside this slice.

Soundscaper desktop-library V11 and selected Framescaper desktop-library V20 each hold one renewable process-lifetime main-owned writer lease in a separate storage scope and database, carrying a persistently monotonic fencing token. Startup waits out an unexpired lease left by a crashed owner, recovers pending prepared, materialized, or committed journals before authenticated renderer admission, and then renews the exact lease while the process is live. Renewal loss fences new admission and publication; shutdown drains admitted work, completes recovery, releases only the exact lease, and closes the database. Soundscaper V11 authenticates project schema 30, SQLite user_version 13 and scope v11; selected S30 inherits established project behavior through exact S29. Framescaper V20 authenticates project schema 31, SQLite user_version 22 and scope v20; its durable idempotent importer opens settled V19 read-only, explicitly reimports exact V28 documents into F31, copies managed bodies exactly, resumes through durable cursor checkpoints, and leaves V19 and its inherited V18, V17 and V12 lineage immutable. Publication uses exact revision and SHA-256 compare-and-swap and passes prepared, materialized, committed, and complete journal checkpoints. The closed matrix executes same-project-simultaneous-open, writer-lease-transfer, stale-lease-takeover, conflicting-canonical-commit, renderer-loss-during-operation, orderly-process-restart, and crash-restart-recovery for both selected products, then runs cross-product-simultaneous-open once against the paired packages to prove V11 and V20 storage and fencing isolation. Qualification can only lower shipped lease TTL and renewal intervals, and journal checkpoints let the runner terminate a process with journal and lease evidence intact. CI is configured to build both unpacked products and emit one bounded no-retry aggregate on Windows x64 and Linux x64. Soundscaper V11 Windows x64, Soundscaper V11 Linux x64, Framescaper V20 Windows x64, and Framescaper V20 Linux x64 remain pending-external; no accepted packaged result is checked in. This control and its gate remain partial; implementation and CI configuration alone do not promote them.

Historical pre-V18 desktop-library V9 and shared schema 17 evidence ran the two frozen Electron workflow IDs through six sequential packaged Soundscaper and Framescaper UI processes: Soundscaper to Framescaper to Soundscaper and Framescaper to Soundscaper to Framescaper. The current CI job is retired and no longer runs these incompatible workflows against Framescaper V18/V10. Each historical workflow owned isolated shared appData and separate product profiles, then returns to its origin profile. Its fixed exact schema 17 project contains one canonical-PCM audio track and clip plus one retained-original VP8 WebM video track and clip that is also represented in the Project Bin. The origin publishes both exact managed bodies. A fresh recipient follows the normal project route into editor activation, hashes the exact Project Bin Blob, starts and stops transport, edits the audio track name through native input, waits for the shared revision 2 save, and invokes the visible Edit in the other product action. The origin return reactivates the exact edited revision and both media bindings. Before the editable project, each fresh recipient also activates two exact-schema-17 read-only role witnesses from the same shared library. Soundscaper to Framescaper covers project-audio-mix-v1 and audio-track-render-v1; Framescaper to Soundscaper covers project-video-render-v1 and video-clip-render-v1. Every recipient witness reaches its role-specific compatibility indicator, starts and stops transport, and invokes the visible cross-product handoff; the feature-requirement read-only state is the only read-only menu exception, while busy and lock-read-only state remains blocked. The origin return opens both witnesses before the mixed-media project, proves the indicator absent and one track-name editor enabled without committing a mutation, and starts and stops transport. The paired aggregate owns audio-whole-mix-electron-roundtrip, audio-track-render-electron-roundtrip, video-full-project-electron-roundtrip, and video-clip-render-electron-roundtrip and requires exact feature, project, requirement, relationship role and fallback source identity plus unchanged canonical-document, canonical-source-body, and fallback-body SHA-256 across recipient and origin. Main-owned handoff-navigation, mixed-media document-digest and binding-ID-and-digest evidence plus strictly increasing catalog revisions and fencing tokens bind all six processes. This qualifies only electron-soundscaper-to-framescaper-to-soundscaper-library and electron-framescaper-to-soundscaper-to-framescaper-library plus those four exact role-return workflow IDs for one fixed small first-party fixture on Linux x64. The web `.scape` workflow matrix is qualified separately. Muted audio does not qualify audible or device output. Packaged activation, fallback playback, unchanged project handoff, and editable origin return are qualified only for the four frozen rendered-fallback roles; packaged rendered-media delivery, fallback authoring and other relationships, general browser or codec behavior, linked or unmanaged media, installers or file associations, concurrency, crash or power loss, Windows, macOS, and ARM64 remain unqualified.

A maintained Chromium browser workflow qualifies the two frozen web `.scape` workflow IDs through three isolated browser contexts in each product order. The origin persists canonical PCM plus one generated WebM and exports the browser-download archive. The witness preserves the exact project ID and verifies every manifest asset body against its declared byte length and SHA-256. A fresh recipient activates both clips, starts and stops transport, makes an undoable track-name edit through native input, invokes explicit save, and exports the return archive. A fresh origin-product context reopens the same identity, asset descriptor set, and edit and starts and stops playback. This fixed small first-party Chromium fixture does not qualify direct File System Access streaming, Firefox, WebKit or Safari, long-form or reference-scale behavior, broad codec coverage, rendered fallbacks, linked or unmanaged media, quota or eviction recovery, crash behavior, or a shared cross-product undo journal.

The explicit handoff is the only shared managed-media publication path; ordinary project saves remain document-only. A writable sender flushes first. A feature-requirement-only intrinsic read-only project may publish its unchanged active snapshot without flushing only while it owns the current writable project lock; declared read-only, future-schema, missing- or stale-lock, and lock-contended projects reject. Before any source body read or bridge call, the sender admits at most 4,094 reachable logical sources, deduplicates compatible same-kind physical bindings, rejects conflicts, and preflights one aggregate 64 GiB audio-and-video byte budget plus the audio-only 65,536-chunk budget. It performs two full validating reads of every canonical-PCM or retained-original-video source; when a binding is absent, the second read also sends at-most-4-MiB chunks through pathless IPC. Main independently caps four active uploads and four active reads across the bridge service, binds sessions to their renderer owner, validates reachable source kind, identity, geometry, and the closed `audio-f32le-chunks-v1` or `video-original-v1` encoding against the exact current project revision, derives the catalog document SHA-256 rather than accepting it from the renderer, and repeats exact revision-and-document-digest validation inside serialized publication. Immutable binding identity includes the project, exact revision, exact document digest, and storage-key/media geometry, so prior-revision media and same-revision document variants are neither advertised nor accepted as present; exact-present reuse requires the declared byte length and SHA-256 and reverifies the regular body. When the exact content already has a different same-kind canonical binding, main may fully verify a donor, create and verify a private random staged hard link, and promote it exclusively to the distinct target. Opaque or corrupt donors are skipped, an exhausted donor can fall through to another, target races never overwrite the winner, recognized unsupported hard-link failures fall back to normal bounded upload, and other operational failures propagate. New uploads remain digest-verified, synced, and atomically renamed before catalog publication. An exact catalog-publication retry for an uploaded or linked materialized target reverifies it and publishes without consuming another offered stream; a retry whose inventory remains planned registers and consumes a new stage/body attempt. After point-in-time capacity admission for an exact-absent binding, and before directory or stage creation, hard-link work, or body consumption, main commits an exact canonical row and random upload or reuse stage to schema-4 authoritative inventory with descriptor provenance and the live lease and fencing token. Promotion accepts only that registered regular stage, atomically renames and directory-syncs it, marks the canonical row materialized, and removes the stage row under persisted before-and-after lease checks. Catalog preparation requires every recognized managed descriptor to have an exact materialized or published row, and catalog commit marks those rows published atomically with metadata. After metadata-journal recovery and project-file reclamation, startup logically retires only tracked descriptors whose exact project ID, revision, and document digest are no longer current, preserves unmanaged or opaque rows, and settles retirement through the normal journal before physical work. A current recognized descriptor without exact materialized or published inventory fails startup before managed-media filesystem mutation. Physical cleanup alternates persisted stage and canonical high-water cycles under a 100,000-total-row startup cap in at-most-64-row lease-fenced transactions; it removes only exact tracked regular stages and canonical bodies through deterministic quarantine, protects current catalog rows, restarts the canonical cursor when eligibility changes, and leaves non-regular, symlinked, unregistered, legacy, and foreign paths untouched. Snapshot counts expose bounded completion, and startup failure releases the lease. Fresh-recipient acquisition performs exact bounded reads into staged audio-source or video-media writers and verifies descriptor identity, kind and storage key, byte length, SHA-256, and canonical audio byte geometry before atomic if-absent publication; opaque retained video is not decoded or probed for media geometry at this boundary. A losing absence race removes only its staging. Pre-shadow rollback conditionally removes only exact acquisition-owned audio records or owned video publications and their source-token, path, or media-chunk payloads, preserving a concurrent replacement; a durable exact shadow commits both kinds before late cancellation is reported. A maintained headless Soundscaper-to-Framescaper edit/save/return fixture proves fresh acquisition, exact PCM engine input, exact Blob video bytes, play/stop state, distinct revision-bound rows with one inode per exact body on the tested Linux filesystem, retained product-local histories, and no bridge or shared-library body read or upload when the original profile reopens. A narrower fixture proves that manifest-only exact-schema role-defined unknown-feature audio fallback PCM crosses from a feature-requirement-only read-only sender that owns the current writable lock and publishes its unchanged active snapshot without flush into an empty recipient with its original and exact shadow before the controller independently verifies the manifest digest and activates exact fallback samples. It then corrupts recipient-local fallback PCM after activation and proves final delivery refuses before render or download; restoring the exact PCM produces the expected fallback samples in WAV output while canonical project state remains unchanged. A role-defined whole-project fixture proves that a feature-requirement-only intrinsically read-only Framescaper sender with the current writable lock transfers an editable retained-video original plus a manifest-only org.example.future-video-pipeline fallback into an empty Soundscaper recipient without flushing the unchanged active snapshot, which acquires both exact video bodies and the exact shadow before the controller independently verifies the manifest digest and activates the exact fallback Blob URL. A distinct clip-target fixture transfers the target canonical video, an unaffected video, and its manifest-only first-party video-effects fallback into a fresh recipient, commits and reopens the exact shadow with the relationship unchanged, rejects wrong-target and whole-project relationship admission, and admits the exact target relationship before playback and delivery replace only the target while preserving the unaffected video. Transfer verifies only each managed descriptor and body digest. The compiled desktop runtime and staging inventory include the managed inventory and collector modules; this does not qualify packaged Electron UI, source-bearing executable workflows, or browser video-codec playback.

An explicitly injected Electron port keeps each linked-audio path and stat identity main-private and exposes only a pathless point-in-time binding. currentControls.summary: Planned and surface-disabled here means the professional hosting surface is not activated, not that no product hosting code exists.
